## Design

### 2026-10-07 – I started designing the PCB today.

**1.5h**

I started designing the PCB today.

I've used circuit boards and soldered them before, but I've never designed something like that. For whatever reason I had KiCad installed already, although I had to update it. Figuring out what all the controls and stuff for the schematic editor was... tedious. But some googling later and I now know about No Connect symbols and how to add and label connections and components. I decided to follow the Starbie Guide as like I said, this is new territory for me. I spent an hour figuring the software out and following the guide, and now I have 5 components diagramed. It honestly felt really good being able to figure this out and get it to make sense, so I feel like I've already learned something.

Here is where I was downloading the starter files and figuring out how to import the needed ones:

### 2026-10-07 – Same day, different session.

**2h**

Same day, different session.

I found some free time, so I decided to work on my Starbie some more. At the end of last session, I finished designing the schematic, minus the footprints, so that's where I picked up. I had to reset my footprint libraries because for whatever reason, the default KiCad one was missing. Small issue though, and we're back on track. I got the footprints all connected and schematic saved and ready for PCB design.

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 193802](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/35b7674a5e50b2632a32abc3a827154bad3692eba46e1031ef38217282be19b0.png)

I had some weird issue when importing the schematic to the PCB editor. It gave me errors, but still imported the PCBs just fine. But, no major catastrophe so onward.

![Screenshot 2026-10-07 200959](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/9pj7FLxKsNBBQr77R6391M1qxl1RKbJZ/e33f9ae9ac6434d3029fa4f2a4a7639c7905daebc1b3c26ddf0266fd10cd8516.png)

Still following the tutorial, I moved on to place the components where they, more or less, should be. It's a little rough, but that just gives it some personality right? Similarly, my art skills were rough too. The star is just special is all. Next I connected the actual wiring and PCB connections, which of course followed the theme thus far: rough. It's messy, but not bad for my first time. I think. I say it is because like I've mentioned: this is the first time I've ever done something like this and used KiCad. So hey, win win. I learned something and designed something.
